check.one-side-key-direct-lake: {{table}}[{{column}}] has to be unique and never blank, or queries that use it fail: {{detail}} relies on it.

check.no-partition: {{table}} has no partition, so it has no data.
check.local-source: {{detail}} reads a file on a computer, which Fabric can refresh only through a gateway.

check.direct-lake-table: {{table}} reads the table {{column}}, which isn’t one Fabricator loaded into the {{detail}} lakehouse.

problem.bad-name: Its folder’s name doesn’t end in .SemanticModel.
problem.unsupported-type: Only semantic models can be supporting items for now, not {{detail}}.
problem.tmsl: It’s defined in model.bim (TMSL). Supporting items are defined in TMDL.
problem.name-mismatch: The name in .platform doesn’t match its folder.
problem.pbism-version: definition.pbism is too old a version for TMDL.
problem.secret: {{file}}, line {{line}}, looks like it holds a credential, such as a password, key or token.
problem.duplicate-table: The table {{table}} is defined more than once.
problem.duplicate-name: {{table}} has more than one column or measure named {{column}}.
problem.duplicate-measure: More than one table has a measure named {{column}}.
problem.missing-table: A relationship refers to the table {{table}}, which the model doesn’t have.
problem.missing-column: A relationship refers to {{table}}[{{column}}], which the model doesn’t have.
problem.self-relationship: A relationship goes from a column to itself.
problem.duplicate-relationship: Two relationships join the same columns.
problem.lakehouse-schemas: lakehouse.metadata.json makes a lakehouse with schemas, which Fabric can’t load tables into yet.
problem.bad-table-name: tables.json names a table {{detail}}: use letters, digits and underscores.
problem.bad-data-path: {{table}} loads from {{detail}}, which isn’t under the lakehouse’s data folder.
problem.empty-data: {{table}} loads from {{detail}}, which has no files.
problem.bad-format: {{table}} loads from {{detail}}, which isn’t CSV or Parquet.
problem.direct-lake-level: Direct Lake tables need compatibility level 1604 or later (it’s {{detail}}).

head.stopped: Stopped before it finished. Blueprint’s Supporting items view shows where each item stands.

card.pickHint: This app isn’t published yet, so choose where its supporting items go. Fabricator remembers it for this app.
card.recreate: It’s gone from Fabric, so it’s created again.
card.drift: Someone changed it in Fabric since Fabricator last applied it. Applying replaces their changes.
card.unapplied: Its folder has changes that aren’t in Fabric yet, so the refresh loads the model as Fabric has it.
card.changesUnknown: Fabricator couldn’t read the model in Fabric, so it can’t show what changes.
card.noChanges: Its tables, columns, measures and relationships stay as they are.
card.credentials: Its data source needs credentials. Set them in the model’s settings in Fabric, then ask Copilot to refresh it again.
card.footnote: Supporting items aren’t part of the Rayfin app. Publish doesn’t change them.
card.noWorkspaces: The app’s Fabric account can’t create items in any shared workspace. Ask a workspace admin for the Contributor role, or create a workspace in Fabric.
card.refreshInFabric: Fabricator can’t start a refresh with your sign-ins. Open the model in Fabric, select Refresh now, then tell Copilot it’s done.
card.lakeEmpty: Its tables.json lists no tables yet, so Fabricator creates it empty.
card.frames: Direct Lake: once it’s applied, Fabricator refreshes it so it reads the lakehouse’s tables.
card.copilotSees: Copilot sees what went wrong too, and tells you what’s next.

view.title: Supporting items
view.subtitle_one: {{count}} item · not part of the Rayfin app
view.subtitle_other: {{count}} items · not part of the Rayfin app
view.intro: The Fabric items this app relies on that aren’t part of the Rayfin app: the semantic models its pages read, and the lakehouses their data is staged in. Copilot defines them in supporting-items/ and changes them in Fabric only after you approve. Publish leaves them alone.
view.emptyOn: Ask Copilot for a semantic model the app needs, such as one over your Snowflake or SQL data, or give it data files to stage in a lakehouse. It asks you before it creates anything in Fabric.
view.emptyOff: Turn them on to let Copilot create the semantic models and lakehouses this app needs. It asks you before each change in Fabric.
view.unavailableTeam: Supporting items aren’t available in team apps.
view.noTarget: New items go to the workspace you choose when Copilot first applies one.
view.signIn: Sign in to Fabric again to see how they stand there.
view.notUsedByApp: Not used by the app yet

prompts.apply: Apply the supporting item {{name}} ({{folder}}) in Fabric with fabricator_apply_supporting_items.
prompts.refresh: Refresh the data of the supporting semantic model {{name}} ({{folder}}) with fabricator_refresh_supporting_item, and tell me how it went.
prompts.connect: Connect the app to the supporting semantic model {{name}} ({{folder}}) with rayfin connector add, check its numbers through the connector, and use it in the app’s pages.

delete.title: Delete {{name}} in Fabric?
delete.message: This deletes the semantic model {{name}} from {{workspace}}. Reports and apps that read it stop working, including this app if it does.
delete.removeFolder: Also move its folder, {{folder}}, to the trash
delete.messageLakehouse: This deletes the lakehouse {{name}} from {{workspace}}, with every file and table in it. Semantic models that read it stop working, and so does this app if it reads one of them.
